sections.title: Building Communications Companies to Create Social Change
sections.description: This interdisciplinary class invites students to 1) understand how world changers have leveraged the forces of capitalism in service of their social change goals; 2) cultivate a personal leadership framework that connects personal passion to public mission to an ethical framework; 3) learn from entrepreneurs that have used media technologies to create companies that change the world and 4) develop ideas for new startups. Students will read inspiring texts from a range of fields (including business, psychology and communications), explore real-world case examples, and hear from entrepreneurs from scaled social purpose ventures (eg: Citizen and Pigeon.ly). Over the semester, students will develop expertise in four key aspects of social changemaking: Mission, Margin, Mandate, and Medium. They will explore actions that serve society (Mission); examine market-based strategies to cultivate healthy, growth-minded organizations that fuel our social fires (Margin); engage with stakeholders regarding the complex social problems in a case-study of their choosing (Mandate); and critically consider the many analog and digital ways to share messages that incite action (Medium).
